Not yet live-tested (setting `GraphicsApi=Vulkan` today would load DXVK for `Direct3DCreate9`, but nothing downstream calls Streamline yet, and DXVK's own real behavior against this specific game hasn't been exercised at all).

**Real safety hardening, same day, before calling this ready to test**: `TryLoadVendoredDxvk()` now validates the loaded DXVK build actually exports `Direct3DCreate9` before committing to it as `g_realD3D9` — without this, a corrupted/wrong-architecture/stale vendored file would still `LoadLibraryA` successfully, then `ResolveRealExports()`'s own existing FATAL-on-missing-export check would fail the ENTIRE DLL init and take the whole game down at launch, not just fail this one feature gracefully. Now falls back to the real system `d3d9.dll` instead, same "always logged, never silently broken, never worse than off" standard this project's every other opt-in feature already meets.

**FIRST LIVE TEST: PASSED, 2026-09-23 — real, huge milestone.** With `GraphicsApi=Vulkan` set live and `iw5sp.exe` launched, the game reaches the real main menu correctly rendered (Special Ops/Campaign/Multiplayer tiles, background art, cursor all rendering normally, no visual corruption) at a stable 60fps/16.6ms frametime — confirmed via a real screenshot, not just a log line. **DXVK's own built-in corner indicator directly confirms Vulkan is the active backend** ("VULKAN 60 FPS 16.6ms" top-left) — independently verified this project's own source prints nothing matching that text anywhere, so this is genuinely DXVK's own identification overlay, not a coincidence or a misread. This is the real go/no-go answer: DXVK's D3D9-to-Vulkan translation DOES work against this specific 2011 IW5 engine build, at least through main-menu rendering — the single biggest open technical risk on the entire Vulkan/DLSS roadmap is now resolved in the affirmative, not theoretical.

**What this does NOT yet confirm, real scope honestly bounded**: only the main menu has been observed — real gameplay (Campaign/Survival loading, in-level rendering, the existing FSR/motion-blur/SMAA full-screen pipeline running on top of a DXVK-backed device, controller input, save/load, menu navigation beyond the main screen) is all still genuinely untested. This project's own existing hooks (`EndScene`/`Reset`/`CreateDevice` vtable hooks) are architecturally expected to keep working unchanged regardless of which library produced the underlying vtable (MinHook operates purely on the in-memory pointer array) — the main-menu result is consistent with that holding, but doesn't prove it holds under load or across a full session. Real next step: play further (load a level, try Survival, exercise the existing visual-enhancement toggles) and watch for any DXVK-specific issue (the real, previously-researched shader-compile-storm pattern this project's own §4.2 research already flagged as a known CoD-lineage-specific DXVK bug class is the standing thing to watch for specifically).

**Real in-level test, same day: a genuine positive AND a genuine open bug.** A direct live report, unprompted: "i gotta say from a frame pacing and smoothness perspective, this is the best the game has ever felt" — a real, notable positive data point independent of DLSS, worth investigating on its own terms later (this project has sunk substantial prior effort into native engine stutter/frame-pacing investigation — the 30Hz-locked-tick characteristic, the render-scale-gated stutter boundary, vsync-pacing issues — and DXVK's own Vulkan present path may simply sidestep some of those D3D9-specific causes structurally; not yet investigated further, flagged for a future pass). **The genuine open bug**: `[Video] MotionBlurEnabled` produces no visible effect at all under `GraphicsApi=Vulkan`, confirmed happening in-level (not just the main menu, directly ruled out) with `[Video] InternalRenderScalePercent` visibly working correctly in the same session — real, DXVK-specific, not a config-toggle miss (`MotionBlurEnabled=1` confirmed in the live ini).

Investigation trail, same day:
1. Added real diagnostic logging (previously silent failure paths): `EnsureMotionBlurShader()` now logs if `CreatePixelShader` ever fails; `RunPreOverlayScenePasses()` now logs the first time `DrawFullScreenPass` is actually reached for motion blur each session. **Result, confirmed via the live log**: `[motion-blur] First DrawFullScreenPass call this session -- gates passed, shader exists, pass is actually running.` — no shader-failure line. This rules out the pass's own gates (menu-active/in-level/clcState, pure native-engine-state reads, unrelated to backend) and shader compilation (DXVK compiles the bytecode fine) as the cause. The bug is downstream: the pass runs every frame, but the visible result never appears.
2. Also found and fixed, same investigation, unrelated to the blur symptom but real: `InitGraphicsApiMode()`'s own log line at `CreateDevice` time unconditionally claimed "Vulkan/DXVK pipeline is not implemented yet -- falling back to LegacyD3D9" even on a session where DXVK had already loaded successfully — stale wording from before DXVK was vendored, not a functional bug (device creation always routed through the right module regardless), but confusing to read. Fixed via a new `g_dxvkActive` flag (`dllmain.cpp`, set on `TryLoadVendoredDxvk()`'s own success path) and `IsDxvkActive()` accessor, so this log now reports ground truth.
3. **Real hypothesis tried and DISPROVEN, do not retry without new evidence**: `DrawFullScreenPass` deliberately calls neither `SetFVF` nor `SetVertexDeclaration` at all — a real, hard-won x86-era finding (issue #100, a 9-round live isolation-test bisection): calling `SetFVF` from this exact function, even perfectly restored afterward, broke the native "you are hurt, get to cover" low-health warning on x86 (theory: the native x86 renderer keeps its own FVF cache separate from the real device state, desynced by this call). **Direct user correction that reopened this as a real x64 candidate**: that native warning is confirmed MISSING from the x64 binary entirely (established 2026-09-14 above — renaming this mod's DLL out of the install directory entirely, zero mod code running, still shows it missing, a genuine Activision regression) — meaning issue #100's specific constraint has nothing left to protect on x64. Re-added `SetFVF(kFVF)` on x64 only (matching the same constant already used safely at four other quad-draw sites in this file), saved/restored, real hypothesis being that DXVK's own from-scratch vertex-state tracking resolves "ambient" FVF differently than a native driver at this point in the frame, potentially pushing the pre-transformed quad through the wrong pipeline. **Live-tested: NO CHANGE, blur still invisible.** Reverted same session per direct instruction ("dont fix what aint broken, setfvf could create unknown issues down the line") — correct call, no confirmed benefit against a real (if same-file-precedented) state-mutation risk. x64 now matches x86 exactly again, no SetFVF/SetVertexDeclaration call from this function on either platform. The x64-vs-x86 constraint difference noted here stays true and on record for a future session, just not acted on since it didn't fix the actual symptom.

**Real, remaining next suspects, not yet tried**: the actual capture step (`StretchRect` from the real backbuffer into `g_fullscreenCaptureTexture`, a same-size/same-format point-filtered copy) or the final composite/blend of the drawn quad — since the pass provably runs and the shader provably compiles, the bug most likely lives in one of these two remaining pieces of `DrawFullScreenPass`'s own pipeline. A genuinely useful, still-untried, zero-code-risk diagnostic: `[Video] SmaaEnabled=1` + `SmaaDebugView=3` ("plain capture-redraw test, no SMAA math") exercises the exact same shared capture/quad-draw path independent of motion blur's own math — if that also shows no visible change (should look identical to off if the pipeline works, since it's a no-op passthrough), it isolates the bug to the shared `DrawFullScreenPass` pipeline itself rather than anything motion-blur-specific; if it looks visibly WRONG, that's a different, more direct signal.

**Second real hypothesis tried and DISPROVEN, 2026-09-23, same session — do not retry without new evidence**: `D3DRS_FOGENABLE` was never saved/restored/disabled by `DrawFullScreenPass`, unlike the four other render states it manages. DXVK's own `UpdateFog()` source has a direct comment flagging exactly this pass's vertex shape (XYZRHW/PositionT, `rhw=1.0` on every vertex) as a genuine W-fog edge case ("PositionT also implies W fog, some D3D6 jank apparently relies on that") — real, source-grounded, not a guess. Added a save/force-off/restore for `D3DRS_FOGENABLE`, matching the function's own existing pattern exactly for the other four states. **Live-tested: NO CHANGE, "confirmed still no-op."** Kept in place regardless (a full-screen post-process pass genuinely has no business being affected by ambient fog state, real correctness fix independent of whether it was ever the actual cause) but ruled out as the explanation for the missing blur.

**Real architecture decision, same day, direct instruction: fork DXVK itself rather than keep guessing against upstream's own unmodified source.** "the dxvk fork is the right call, were not remaking dxvk, were fitting it into iw5s engine." `doitsujin/dxvk` forked to `github.com/k8se10/MW32011DXVK` and merged into this repo as a real, history-preserving `git subtree` at `dxvk/` (full real DXVK commit history preserved as a second parent, same pattern as `security/`/`tools/iw5oat`, not squashed — see `CLAUDE.md`'s own "Nested components" entry for the full record). **Explicitly scoped, not a rebuild**: the goal is to identify and patch the real, specific MW3/IW5-engine quirk causing this exact invisible-motion-blur symptom directly in DXVK's own source, not to maintain a general-purpose DXVK fork or rebuild DXVK from scratch. **Real standalone-release requirement, direct instruction**: "this repo should also be treat as standalone from ncp as it will get it own releases despite being nested, this means it must not be ncp reliant or native reliant. it must be smart and know what version its being run on so it doesnt mess up the hooks" — `MW32011DXVK` gets its own independent version/release cadence (not tied to NCP's own `-x64` version numbers), must not depend on any NCP-specific code/headers, and must be able to run standalone (not assume it's only ever loaded alongside NCP's own native pipeline). The real, concrete technical requirement this implies: any MW3/IW5-specific patch this fork ever adds must be gated behind a genuine runtime detection of which game binary/build it's actually running against (the same real problem NCP's own `game_exe_detect.h` already solves for its own hooks, `iw5sp.exe`/`iw5mp.exe`, likely needing an equivalent, independent mechanism inside DXVK itself) — so an IW5-specific quirk-workaround can never silently misfire against an unrelated game/build DXVK might also be loaded into, and so DXVK-side patches can't interfere with NCP's own hooks by assuming context that isn't actually there. Not yet implemented — real groundwork/scope decision, recorded here and in the fork's own repo for continuity. Full technical Meson/build-toolchain setup (this project's existing build is pure MSVC/vcxproj, DXVK's own is Meson-based) is real, separate, not-yet-started follow-up work before any actual custom DXVK build can happen.

It didn't. This conclusively rules out DXVK/the Vulkan backend and reframes the bug as pure `MW32011NCP` game-logic, unrelated to which D3D9 backend is active.

**Real root cause**: `analog_input_hooks_x64.cpp`'s `Hook_MovementTick`, commit `fa3ae124f` ("fix: make motion blur react to real per-tick view-angle change, not controller-only", same day, earlier). That commit replaced the original controller/gyro-only direct delta writes (`g_motionBlurYawDeltaDegX64`/`PitchDeltaDegX64` set directly from the computed `yawDelta`/`pitchDelta`/`gyroYawDelta`/`gyroPitchDelta` values) with a single universal pre/post-`g_realMovementTick()` diff of the look accumulators (`preNativeYaw - *g_yawAccum` etc.), reasoning that the native accumulate-then-pack-with-fractional-remainder step would preserve ANY contributor's delta the same way. Real, live-tested result: this genuinely fixed K+M (previously always zero, since real mouse look happens entirely inside the native trampoline this file never otherwise touches) but broke controller (previously working, confirmed via the same commit's own diff against the prior working code). Working hypothesis, consistent with all evidence: a large single-tick controller-stick delta (up to `lookDegreesPerSecondHorizontal`/`Vertical`, tick-scaled -- routinely much larger than a natural mouse-motion delta) does not round-trip through the native compressed usercmd angle-pack step the same cleanly as the small deltas real mouse motion produces, so the diff under-reports the true controller-intended delta; real mouse deltas, always small, round-trip fine, which is exactly why K+M alone (diff-only, before this fix) already worked.

**Fix, hybrid capture, implemented and live-tested working (user: "fixed")**: `Hook_MovementTick` now tracks its OWN directly-known controller/gyro delta this tick (`controllerYawDeltaThisTickX64`/`controllerPitchDeltaThisTickX64`, `controllerContributedThisTickX64`, set inside the existing stick-input and gyro blocks -- the exact byte-for-byte pre-`fa3ae124f` values, not re-derived from any native round-trip) and, after the native call, uses those DIRECT values for `g_motionBlurYawDeltaDegX64`/`PitchDeltaDegX64` whenever the stick or gyro contributed this tick -- restoring the proven-correct controller behavior exactly. Only falls back to the pre/post-native-call diff when neither contributed (pure real mouse/keyboard motion, the case the diff technique is actually proven correct for). Real, accepted minor limitation: a player moving both controller stick and mouse in the exact same tick (unusual hybrid setup) only gets the controller-direct value that tick, silently dropping mouse's own separate contribution -- not the reported bug, not worth the added complexity to close. Build-verified (x64 Release, 0 errors, `dumpbin`-confirmed genuine x64 output), deployed live, **user-confirmed fixed same day.**

**REVISED, later the same day -- the actual jitter WRITE is genuinely blocked, not just unstarted, after a full decompile.** A follow-up fork fully decompiled `FUN_1401e13e0` (not just its prologue) and mapped all 16 floats it writes: Row0/Row1 confirmed exactly as the live diagnostic already showed (X-scale/Y-scale), but **Row2 (`+0x14f0`) is entirely zero and Row3 (`+0x1500`) packs near/far terms plus two hardcoded `1.0f` sentinels** -- a genuinely nonstandard layout, not the textbook D3D9 `[0,0,zf/(zf-zn),1]`/`[0,0,-zn*zf/(zf-zn),0]` row2/row3 shape this project's own earlier plan assumed. This means the standard "jitter goes into the oblique `M[2][0]`/`M[2][1]` terms" convention cannot be assumed to transfer here -- writing into the currently-zero Row2 slots has no evidence the vertex shader even reads Row2 at all. **A real correction found in the same pass**: `+0x1490` (round 3's own lead, the WORLD-combine's second operand) turned out to be a static constant-table copy, unrelated to the real per-frame camera matrix -- the correct matrix was `+0x14d0`/`+0x1510` all along, exactly what the diagnostic hook already validates live; nothing shipped was affected, this only corrects the round-3 writeup. Viewport width/height (needed for the Halton(2,3) phase-count formula) are confirmed available from `FUN_1401df1b0`'s own output, ready to use once the write target is resolved. **Genuine blocker, not a "try harder" situation**: the safe jitter offset can't be determined by more static decompiling -- it needs either a live RenderDoc/PIX frame capture or SM3 vertex-shader bytecode disassembly, neither of which this project has ever set up. Honestly reported rather than risking a write that could corrupt live render state.

**Real, in-house alternative shipped same day instead of standing up new tooling, then iterated live through several real rounds**: rather than RenderDoc/PIX, `Hook_ProjectionMatrixBuild` got a strictly opt-in `[Video] ProjectionMatrixJitterProbeEnabled` mode (default off, developer/RE-verification only). The mechanism went through real, live-tested revisions:
- **v1 (timed auto-cycle, accumulating `+=`, no undo)**: live-tested, produced dramatic, unmistakable visible distortion on 4 of 8 candidates (Row0[2]/[3], Row1[2]/[3] -- real screen-space "warp speed" streaking and TV-static-style noise, screenshots captured) and confirmed ZERO effect on Row2[0] even at this same mechanism -- real, decisive live evidence Row2 is genuinely unread by the shader, matching the earlier full-decompile finding.
- **A real methodological trap found and corrected mid-session**: the "fix" (undo-before-reapply every fire, properly bounding the perturbation to a single frame's value, escalated through amplitudes 0.25 -> 8.0 -> 200.0) produced literally NO visible effect at any amplitude -- a real, sharp user correction settled why: since the v1 accumulating bug clearly DID reach the GPU (visible distortion proves it), an "upload path never re-reads this struct" theory is wrong; the real explanation is that a naive `+=` with no undo, firing every hook call with no bound, random-walks into the TENS-to-HUNDREDS within seconds (a dense per-frame sum of sine samples does not stay near its nominal amplitude) -- v1's "0.25 amplitude" was never actually 0.25 in practice.
- **REVISED, direct user instruction: back to the known-working v1 mechanism (accumulating, no undo), but one fixed candidate per process launch (`ProjectionMatrixJitterProbeCandidateIndex`, 0-7) instead of an automatic timed cycle** -- a fresh relaunch per candidate guarantees no state carries over, "slower but clean every single time."
- **A real, CRITICAL launch-crash self-inflicted in this same session, found and fixed via live crash-dump analysis (WinDbg/mcp-windbg, the standing-approved static technique)**: `buf[220]` for the new single-candidate log line was already ~219 bytes consumed by the literal format text alone, guaranteeing a real `sprintf_s` overflow (`FAST_FAIL_INVALID_ARG`) on every launch with the probe enabled -- the exact same recurring buffer-overflow bug class this project has now hit multiple times, this time self-inflicted while building THIS feature. Fixed (widened to 400, plus a proactive fix on a second close-call buffer in the same area, 256->400). A 25-second startup delay was also added (direct user request) so the probe only ever activates once gameplay is reached, never during loading/menu.
- Build-verified (x64 Release, 0 errors, genuine x64 confirmed via `dumpbin`) after every change, deployed. This is real, empirical, human-observed live testing (screenshots captured for the v1 mechanism, confirming 5 of 8 candidates directly), matching this project's own established "verify live" bar -- not guesses shipped as fixes. Full trail: `vulkan_dlss_pipeline_research.md` item 2.
