## 10. Native x64 audio-duplication/echo theory during combat -- real internal sound-alias play/blend function found and instrumented; diagnostic hook shipped, not yet live-tested

**Status: Investigating.** Direct user report and explicit scope correction, 2026-09-26, following a pasted external analysis (a separate ChatGPT conversation) suggesting the severe reported lag might be explained by duplicated/echoing audio during combat rather than a rendering-side cause. An initial pass wrongly investigated this project's OWN runtime code first (Fire/ADS notify-dispatch, damage rumble) and found no obvious duplicate-trigger candidate there. **The user forcefully corrected this framing, verbatim: "NOT NCP SIDE DUMBASS int tyhe x64 gME ITSELF, REMEMBER udioo was remastered here clear as day"** -- the investigation is scoped to the NATIVE x64 game binary's own audio system, not this mod's code, and the user asserts (their own claim, not yet independently verified by this project) that the audio system was substantively changed/remastered as part of the 2026-09-03 x64 recompile.

**Real, independent corroborating signal already on record in this project's own research (issue #8, above)**: a separate Reddit poster (`vlad_ruble`) is quoted as reporting the x64 update "broke some sound playback" -- a real, pre-existing, independent report of a native audio regression on this exact binary, not something invented for this investigation.

**Real native function found and mapped**: a Ghidra string-xref search for "sound" turned up a cluster of real internal sound-engine diagnostic/warning strings (`"attempted to play spatialized alias '%s' while there is no active listener..."`, and a full family of `"tried to blend between sound aliases '%s' and '%s', but they don't use the same <X>"` mismatch warnings covering channel/volume-falloff/looping/priority/etc.) -- these are real, native `S_StartSound`/alias-blend engine internals, not GSC-side. The first warning's own two xrefs led to **`FUN_140274100`**, the real native sound-alias play/blend function -- full decompile confirms: it does the actual spatialization math (listener-relative distance/occlusion, Doppler-style pitch/volume blend), looks up channel-priority-eviction candidates, and -- notably -- recursively re-invokes itself (via `FUN_140273ec0`) to chain into a `secondaryAliasName`/`chainAliasName` on the same `snd_alias_t` entry, real, intentional multi-alias-blend behavior, capped at a real depth limit (`FUN_140273ec0`'s own `param_11 < 0xb` check, i.e. max 11 chained levels) -- so recursion itself is NOT evidence of a bug on its own; a real duplicate-playback bug would show as rapid repeated top-level (depth==0) plays of the SAME alias name, not a normal depth>0 chain.

**Diagnostic hook shipped (read-only, log-and-call-through, zero behavior change)**: `Hook_PlaySoundAlias` (`proxy_d3d9/src/analog_input_hooks_x64.cpp`), a real MinHook detour on `FUN_140274100` via a hand-corrected signature (`kPlaySoundAliasSignature` -- `DumpSigBytes.java`'s own heuristic over-flagged several `[RAX+offset]` stack-relative stores as needing wildcards, per this project's own already-documented false-positive with that tool; only the one real RIP-relative global-flag check and the one real conditional-jump rel32 are actually wildcarded). Logs the first 200 fires unconditionally (to catch a real combat burst whole, not truncated by an early rate-limit), then falls back to this file's own standard ~250ms floor. Per fire: the alias name (SEH-guarded read off the asset's own first field, bounded print via `%.48s` -- deliberately defensive against this project's own repeated sprintf_s-overflow bug class, four prior incidents), channel, and the real recursion-depth argument. SP-only (this function was only ever verified against `iw5sp_x64_full`'s own Ghidra project; `InstallAnalogInputHooksX64()` is already called only under the confirmed-`iw5sp.exe` branch in `dllmain.cpp`). Build-verified (x64 Release, 0 errors, deployed live -- `d3d9.dll` timestamp confirmed changed, avoiding this project's own known "build silently no-ops" trap). **Not yet live-tested** -- the next real step is a combat playtest watching `proxy_d3d9.log` for `[x64-sound-diag] PlaySoundAlias fire` lines, specifically checking for the SAME alias name firing repeatedly at `depth=0` within a tight time window (the concrete signature that would confirm the duplicate-playback theory) versus normal, expected `depth>0` chain-blend traffic.

### Static x86-vs-x64 diff, 2026-09-26 -- the core play/blend function and its chain-alias recursion mechanism are structurally IDENTICAL between architectures; no regression found in this specific subsystem

**Status: Investigating (narrowed).** Direct instruction: "we should staticaly diff to see if its a regression between binaries." Found the real x86 equivalent of `FUN_140274100` by searching the x86 Ghidra project for the exact same "attempted to play spatialized alias" warning string -- it resolves to a two-function pair, `FUN_006b2580` (the small "no active listener" branch helper) and its only caller `FUN_006b2e00` (the real outer play/blend function, matching x64's `FUN_140274100` structurally field-for-field: same distance-cull gate, same channel-priority-eviction loops, same final dispatch-by-listener-mode branch, same trailing unconditional recursive call for chain-alias blending).

**The recursion/depth-cap mechanism -- the single most obvious a-priori suspect for a "plays the same sound N times in a row" bug -- is confirmed logically IDENTICAL, not just similar**: x86's `FUN_006b2c90` (the recursion gate, called with `param_10+1` each time) uses the exact same real guard chain as x64's `FUN_140273ec0` (chain-target-exists check, target-resolves check, a symmetric listener-flag match check, then the depth test) and both cap recursion at the identical `param_N < 0xb` (11 levels). This mechanism was ported faithfully -- it is not the source of any duplicate-playback regression.

**Caller-count discrepancy investigated and resolved as a false lead**: x64's own caller list for `FUN_140274100` initially showed 15 references vs x86's 10 for `FUN_006b2e00` -- 3 of the x64 references (`144458a3c`, `1404a6520`, `1404a6574`) turned out to be `.pdata` (x64 SEH exception-unwind table, `RUNTIME_FUNCTION` `{BeginAddress, EndAddress, UnwindInfoAddress}` triples) self-references, not real code callers -- confirmed via a raw dword dump of that region showing the exact expected table shape (each function's own start/end address pairs). x86 has no such table at all (different, frame-based exception model), which fully explains the raw count gap on its own -- once corrected, x64 has 12 real callers (including its own recursion self-call) vs x86's 10 (including its own), a real but modest difference (11 vs 9 non-recursion wrapper callers). Bulk-decompiled all 11 real x64 non-recursion callers: each is a distinct, purpose-built thin parameter-forwarding shim (positioned play, local play, entity-attached play, two separate scheduled-sound-queue flush loops over two DIFFERENT global arrays) -- no pair of them share a body or dispatch the same queue twice; no smoking-gun duplicate-call wrapper found by inspection.

**Honest scope of what this clears and what it doesn't**: this rules out the play/blend function itself and its chain-alias recursion as the mechanism behind a reported echo/duplicate-audio symptom, on this specific subsystem, from static reading alone. It does NOT clear the game's audio system as a whole -- the real regression (if the symptom is real and native, not this mod's own code, per the user's own explicit framing) is more likely either (a) in whatever decides to CALL one of these wrapper functions in the first place (an entity-event/FX-trigger table, or a GSC builtin dispatch path, neither traced yet), or (b) in a genuinely separate audio subsystem entirely (streamed dialogue/music, which doesn't route through `snd_alias_t` chain-blending at all). The live diagnostic hook shipped earlier this session (`Hook_PlaySoundAlias`, `[x64-sound-diag]` log lines) remains the real next data point -- a live combat capture showing (or not showing) rapid same-alias repeats at `depth=0` is still the most direct way to confirm or rule out this specific mechanism in practice, independent of what the static read above already shows.

### Real, separate lead found, 2026-09-26 -- a native sun/cascade-shadow fast-vs-slow dispatcher, keyed off distinct dvars from the already-fixed per-light shadow loop; a live diagnostic hook shipped to confirm which path sun-ray maps are actually taking

**Status: Investigating.** Direct user observation, from a longer multi-map test: "i think ik wha is making the lag, sun rays [screenshot of Dome, Wave 1, visible light shafts through a broken skylight] only maps with sun rays like this so far have been obsertved with the 4x slowdown." This is a real, independently-derived correlation from the user's own testing, separate from anything this project had already traced.

**Found a genuinely distinct native shadow subsystem, not the same mechanism as the already-fixed per-light point/spot-light loop.** A string-xref search for sun/shadow-related identifiers turned up a real, separate dvar family with the `sm_` (shadow-map) prefix -- `sm_sunShadowCenter`, `sm_sunShadowCenterMode`, `sm_sunShadowScale`, `sm_fastSunShadow`, `sm_sunShadowScaleLocked` -- registered in the same master render-dvar function (`FUN_1401b50e0`) as the already-known `r_light*`/`SkipRedundantShadowActivation`-adjacent dvars, but consumed by entirely different code (traced via `FindGlobalRefs.java`). The real per-frame dispatcher, `FUN_14019c450`, does a clean two-way branch based on `sm_fastSunShadow`'s live value (confirmed at registration to default TRUE) and a second, not-yet-identified per-frame flag at a fixed offset into a large global state block (`DAT_141896b80 + 0x41a5c`): when `sm_fastSunShadow` is on AND that flag is 0, it calls `FUN_14019b520` (the real FAST path, matching the dvar's own name/intent); every other case falls through to `FUN_14019b960` (the slow/full-quality fallback). This dispatcher itself is gated behind a real per-frame visibility check (`FUN_1401d2b20`, called from the shadow-pipeline state machine `FUN_1401d6ed0`) -- consistent with it only running when the sun is actually relevant to the current view, exactly the condition a map with visible light shafts through windows/skylights would satisfy far more consistently than a map without a strong directional sun.

**Two real, distinct hypotheses this could confirm, not yet distinguished**: (1) this is simply genuinely expensive-by-design work, correctly gated on sun visibility, and sun-heavy maps are just more expensive by nature -- not a bug at all, just real content cost (the same "proportional content scaling" conclusion already reached for Dome-vs-Underground's per-light transition counts); or (2) something on x64 is causing this dispatcher to take the SLOW path (`FUN_14019b960`) even when it shouldn't -- a wrong `sm_fastSunShadow` default, a stuck/miscalculated flag at `DAT_141896b80+0x41a5c`, or a genuine x64-recompile regression in this specific subsystem, unrelated to anything this project has already found or fixed for issue #4.

**Diagnostic hook shipped (read-only, log-and-call-through, zero behavior change, uncapped per direct instruction -- "these are dev test toggles not mod features to keep on")**: `Hook_SunShadowDispatch` (`proxy_d3d9/src/analog_input_hooks_x64.cpp`), a MinHook detour on `FUN_14019c450` via a hand-corrected 71-byte signature (`kSunShadowDispatchSignature`). Resolves both governing globals (the flag base and the `sm_fastSunShadow` dvar handle) via `SigScan::ResolveRipRelative` at fixed, known offsets within the same signature match, per this file's own established technique -- SEH-guarded reads, defaults to a clearly-labeled "read-failed" state rather than guessing. Logs every fire: the flag's live value, the dvar's live bool, which path was actually selected (by name), and a tick timestamp. SP-only (same gating as every other hook in this file). Build-verified (x64 Release, 0 errors, `d3d9.dll` timestamp confirmed changed), deployed live. **Not yet live-tested** -- the real next step is reproducing on the same sun-ray map (Dome, per the screenshot) and reading `proxy_d3d9.log` for `[x64-sunshadow-diag] dispatch fire` lines: a session dominated by `path=SLOW(FUN_14019b960)` on a sun-ray map would be strong, concrete confirmation of hypothesis (2) above; a session that's genuinely gated to low-frequency fires with the FAST path selected would instead point back toward hypothesis (1) (real content cost, not a bug) and redirect investigation back to characterizing exactly what `FUN_14019b960`/the cascade tile sizes (0x1800x0x400 and 0x3000x0x800, per the decompile) actually cost when they do run.
